headline: Bohm's 15th homer not enough as Braves top Phillies 5-2
recap: The Braves scored three times in the top of the second Friday night, an inning that started with Austin Riley's RBI single driving in Lane Thomas on a play aided by a fielding error on right fielder Bryce Harper, continued with Ha-Seong Kim's run-scoring groundout that brought in Mauricio Dubón, and finished with Ronald Acuña Jr.'s single scoring Riley for a 3-0 lead. The Phillies got one back in the bottom of the second on an Alec Bohm double that scored Luis Arraez, then Bohm cut the deficit to 3-2 in the fourth with his 15th home run of the season. Atlanta answered in the top of the eighth when Mauricio Dubón hit his 11th homer, a two-run shot that also scored Mike Yastrzemski, and the Braves closed it out from there for a 5-2 win at Citizens Bank Park. Cristopher Sánchez took the loss, allowing three runs on five hits over six innings, and Orion Kerkering surrendered the eighth-inning homer; Chris Sale worked six innings and struck out seven for the win, with Raisel Iglesias closing it out for the save. Bohm finished 2-for-4 with the homer, a double and two RBIs, and Arraez added two hits.
The loss dropped the Phillies to 79-62, second in the NL East, five games behind the division-leading Braves, and now on a two-game losing streak.

Philadelphia and Atlanta play the third game of their series Saturday at Citizens Bank Park, with Zack Wheeler starting for the Phillies opposite the Braves' Martín Pérez. First pitch is scheduled for 6:06 PM ET. DraftKings has the Phillies as -163 moneyline favorites, with Philadelphia at -1.5 on the run line (+129).
